info.title: Lenipo API
info.description: REST API of Lenipo. Browsers authenticate with the session cookie; scripts, the CLI and MCP clients with a personal access token (`Authorization: Bearer tl_pat_…`).

get.summary: Show version, runtime and database information

get.description: Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Import from Jira Server/DC
post.description:
Starts a job in the worker. With dryRun (the default) it reads everything and reports what it would create, map and skip, without writing. Project keys must be free in Lenipo. Objects imported before are skipped, so a second run adds only new ones. The token is kept only while the job runs.

Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Import a Confluence Server/DC space export
post.description:
The space XML export as a ZIP (field "file"). Pages with their versions, blog posts, comments, attachments and labels; Confluence macros become Lenipo macros where one exists. `spaceKey` names the new space (the export's key by default); dryRun (the default) only reports.

Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Import a project or space archive of another Lenipo
post.description:
The ZIP from "Export as archive" (field "file"). Everything gets new ids; people are matched by e-mail or created deactivated, issue types, statuses, priorities and link types by key or name. `targetKey` renames the project or space; dryRun (the default) only reports.

Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Import what a dry run checked
post.description:
Starts the real import with the file uploaded for the dry run (Confluence or archive).

Requires the global permission `admin`.

post.summary: Change many issues at once
post.description: Edit, transition, move to a sprint, delete, watch or unwatch. Each issue goes through the same checks as a single change; the result lists which failed and why.

post.summary: Create up to 100 issues
post.description: Each issue goes through the same checks as POST /issues. The result has one line per issue in the order sent. With "atomic": true they are created in one transaction: all or none.

post.summary: Change up to 100 issues, each in its own way
post.description: Each change goes through the same checks as PATCH /issues/{key}. With "atomic": true all or none are made.

post.summary: Copy an issue
post.description: Copies fields, custom fields and the security level, links the copy to the original ("clones"), and optionally the subtasks. Needs create-issues.

post.summary: Move an issue with its subtasks to another project
post.description: New keys, the old ones keep working. Type and status are kept where the target allows, else mapped (same category, else initial); components and versions by name; security level kept or the target default. Needs edit-issues in the source and create-issues in the target.

post.summary: Restore an issue from the trash
post.description: Brings back the subtasks deleted with it too. Needs delete-issues.

The project's workflow for the editor
get.description: Statuses in order, the initial status, allowed moves and how many issues use each status. With `issueType`, the workflow of that issue type: its own, or the standard one it uses (`inherited`).

post.summary: Publish a new version of the project workflow
post.description: Needs project administration. The first edit gives the project its own copy of a shared workflow; with `issueType`, the first edit gives that issue type a workflow of its own. The issues it applies to move to the new version; issues on removed statuses take the status given in `migrate` (history entry, no notifications); boards of the project adjust their columns. Answers 409 when `baseVersionId` is no longer current.

put.summary: Save the shared draft of a workflow
put.description: Needs project administration. One draft per project and issue type (`issueType`, else the standard workflow), shared by its administrators; publishing removes it (TL-77).

delete.summary: Discard the draft of a workflow
Let an issue type use the standard workflow again
delete.description: Needs project administration. Issues of the type keep their status where the standard workflow has it, else take the first status of the same category or the initial status (history entry, no notifications).
